subject: Why do two Zero-Inflated Poisson models that fit the same data but in different ways with INLA, estimate the parameters differently?

messages.author: 8a32ef327d69b4f6
messages.subject: Why do two Zero-Inflated Poisson models that fit the same data but in different ways with INLA, estimate the parameters differently?
parts:
Hi everyone!
I am trying to fit a ZIP model using INLA with two linear predictors, one for the binomial part, and another one for the Poisson part. I have tried to fit the simplest model (just intercept in both cases). We have conducted it in two different ways:
- (M1) I fit a model with the Zero-Inflated Poisson family that INLA has by default ("zeroinflatedpoisson1"), and
- (M2) I fit it as a joint likelihood using a binomial and a ZIP families (following the advanced example in the documentation).
Both models fit the same ZIP simulated data. The point is that results are different for the binomial part and I was wondering why in the case of the joint likelihood is not working as I was expecting.
I attach a Rmd and a HTML with the developed code in case it is helpful.
Many thanks!
Oihane.

parts:
you can only do the 'joint' model trick if the poisson part separates
the zero's, so you have

p * 1[y==0] + (1-p) * f(y | y > 0)

without the '|y>0' then do you not know which component a zero comes
from
